The suspect, who has not been named, forced his way into Silver Rail Elementary School in the city of Bend on Thursday afternoon by shooting at locked doors, Bend Police Chief Mike Krantz confirmed. The teenager was shot dead by a community member who "pursued him into the school and engaged him", Krantz said. Police arrived three minutes later. The three children killed were aged five, eight and 11. A seven-year-old and a 54-year-old teacher were taken to a hospital in a critical condition. It is unclear if the attacker had any links to the school. The suspect was shot dead moments after local law enforcement arrived at the scene "We are stunned and heartbroken by this senseless tragedy," Steven Cook, the top administrative official of the local school district, said in a statement. "No words can adequately express the grief our community is experiencing." Police said the attacker was a local 16-year-old boy, but they did not release any further details on him or the identity of the victims. Police were alerted to an active shooter at Silver Rail Elementary at 12:59 local time (19:59 GMT), Bend Police Department spokeswoman Sheila Miller told reporters. The first call came from a person who said that an unknown suspect was shooting into their car with a long gun, police said. Photos released from the scene show a red truck with bullet holes. Minutes later, the local county dispatch received 911 calls reporting that the attacker had entered the school. Police said he shot at locks on the doors in order to force his way inside. Local media reports suggested the school received new classroom doors in 2022 which can be locked with the flip of a switch. A bystander saw the shooting begin to unfold, pursued the attacker into the school and shot him dead, police explained. Three minutes later, officers first arrived at the scene. clusters.text: The White House is defending its new press secretary, Katie Zacharia, as she faces scrutiny over her legal credentials. President Donald Trump described Zacharia as an attorney when announcing her appointment last week. She has referred to herself as a lawyer. But when she was asked on Tuesday by a reporter in which state she had passed the bar exam required to be an attorney in the US, she said standing alongside the president: "When I moved to China." She does not appear to be registered to the bar in any state where she has lived. White House communications director Steven Cheung said Zacharia is "uniquely qualified and whip smart to help inform the American people". Responding to questions about her credentials, Zacharia said in a statement this week: "I practised international transaction law, with all the appropriate credentials." On Wednesday, a watchdog group, Campaign for Accountability, filed a complaint with the California State Bar Association. It is seeking an investigation into whether Zacharia "repeatedly held herself out to the public as entitled to practise law without a licence to do so, conduct California law treats as a crime". The 42-year-old political strategist graduated from law school at Pepperdine University in California in 2011, the university confirmed. The new White House press secretary told the New York Times on Wednesday that when she first began appearing on cable news, she had asked Pepperdine how she should identify herself. She said she was advised by the university president that she could call herself a lawyer, but not an attorney. The new press secretary also told the paper that when she answered China to a question about her bar exam, it was a misunderstanding. She had mistakenly thought, above the din of Marine One, the reporter had asked: "Where were you after law school?" Zacharia took the bar exam in California after graduating from law school but did not pass, according to the Wall Street Journal. California's bar exam is widely regarded as one of the hardest in the US to pass. A person with direct knowledge of the matter told the outlet that Zacharia took the exam around the same time that she was planning a wedding and preparing to move to China with her husband-to-be. US President Donald Trump said on Thursday that the execution of Fort Hood shooter Nidal Malik Hasan will not be livestreamed . The announcement comes after the Trump administration faced criticism from both Republicans and Democrats, as well as rights groups and many in the international community. Vice President JD Vance also said he would not watch such a livestream. Trump wrote on his social media platform Truth Social that publicly airing the execution “might have been a strong deterrent for the World to witness how America deals with Terrorists and SCUM like Hasan." But the president added that "any very good and well meaning people would rather not watch him die, through streaming, or through any other visual device." Trump said he "will die, as scheduled, by firing squad, but this event will not be streamed." He noted that the execution can be viewed in person by immediate families of the victims, "if they so choose." Hasan's execution is scheduled for Deccember 3 at the US military prison in Fort Leavenworth, Kansas. The public execution idea drew wide condemnation from lawmakers of both main US parties, Republicans and Democrats, including top House Republican Mike Johnson, who said it could be a "recruiting tool for future terrorists." Dozens of retired US military officers also published an open letter warning against broadcasting the execution, saying it "will taint the honor of the military that employs it, and a nation that allows it." The letter added that such a move woud "ensure that Hasan becomes a martyr for attacking and killing his fellow soldiers," said the officers, including more than 40 generals and admirals. When asked about the public execution and whether it was acceptable in his Christian faith, Vance said he didn't know that it would actually happen. Serbian tennis player Stefan Milicevic has been given a 24-year ban for allegedly fixing multiple matches and recruiting other players into a “corrupt network,” the International Tennis Integrity Agency (ITIA) said Thursday. The agency said the 29-year-old Milicevic was charged with fixing six matches including five of his own and trying to fix six more between 2022 and 2024. He is banned from tennis until 2050. Milicevic never reached a singles ranking higher than 1,338 and only played in lower tier events. But the ITIA also charged him with recruiting “multiple professional players as part of a corrupt network” that resulted in “a number of other players fixing matches” during those same years. The agency did not give details about which matches were fixed, or name any of the other players involved. It said Milicevic did not cooperate into its investigation into the fixed matches and did not respond to its findings. It also fined Milicevic USD 70,000.

clusters.title: Apple consolidates smart-home capabilities in HomeView dashboard
clusters.text: Technology company Apple has released a screen that consolidates the functions of its app products and its home-management software into one device. HomeView is a seven-inch display meant to function as a centralised location for home controls, signalling a step forward in Apple 's home integration and smart home services. The screens come in two versions. One sits on its own, standing on a base with an integrated speaker, while the other is wall-mounted. HomeView works similarly to other Apple touchscreen products, with a home screen, apps, widgets and a built-in front-facing camera. It has many of the same functions, including FaceTime video calling. The product creates a physical dashboard for the Apple Home app, which was released in 2022 to control integrated functions such as smart locks, appliances, cameras and thermostats. HomeView uses face recognition for up to six people per device in a household with personalised settings for each user, instead of the app sitting on personalised devices. The product also includes an intercom system that can connect multiple devices within one household. The tabletop version of the device has a distinct form, with a case and a thick base made from recycled aluminium. Its rounded base and movable screen evoke the design of the 2002 iMac G4 desktop computer. Apple emphasised the device's potential as decor, calling it "the perfect addition to a kitchen counter, nightstand, or side table." It comes in four colour options: silver, starlight, rose pink, and space grey.

also: Bank deposits hit record $3 trillion, boosted by dollar deposits scheme
clusters.text: India's banking system deposits hit a record high of around 284 trillion rupees ($2.99 trillion) in the second half of September, central bank data showed on Thursday. Deposits rose by 21.67 trillion rupees in the first six months of the financial year, with most of the increase seen between June and August, when the central bank's discounted swap window to attract dollar inflows was in place. Banking system deposits jumped by an aggregate of 20 trillion rupees from June 16 to August 31, according to data from the Reserve Bank of India. In June, the RBI announced a discounted swap window to attract foreign-currency deposits and encouraged lenders to raise cheaper deposits. The scheme saw inflows of around $133 billion and the deposit window was closed on August 31, a month earlier than planned. Deposits were also boosted by lenders' efforts to build funding buffers before the end of the quarter; the fortnight ended September 30 saw inflows of 7.73 trillion rupees. Overall deposits in the banking system as of September-end were up 8.4 per cent as compared with March-end.Competition for deposits stayed contained, while the system was in surplus, CareEdge Ratings said in a note. "The October rate hike rules out further cuts in term deposit rates for now and is likely to push them up, as banks need to fund credit that is growing faster than deposits while the liquidity surplus shrinks," CareEdge added.

The 24-year-old Briton, who missed more than six months with a stress fracture in her back, beat Ukrainian Svitolina 6-2 2-6 6-4 to mark her sixth win in eight matches since returning from injury. It was another eye-catching performance by Kartal, who defeated Italian 15th seed Jasmine Paolini and Swiss ninth seed Belinda Bencic in the previous rounds. She will face 2017 French Open champion Jeļena Ostapenko, who came through a tense opening set to beat 11th seed Diana Shnaider 7-6 (8-6) 6-1, in her first WTA 1000 semi-final on Saturday. Speaking on court after her victory, Kartal said she knew "what a great fighter" world number six Svitolina is, so she "was never safe" in the match. "It was solid composure from me throughout," she added. "It's breaking new ground for me this week. "I love playing here and on this court. The atmosphere was amazing, so big thank you to the crowd." Kartal had not dropped a set during her run to the quarter-finals at Wuhan, and she broke Svitolina early in the first to start on a positive note. Svitolina then called for a medical timeout for treatment on her right arm, but she came back strong to take the second set 6-2 and send the last-eight tie to a decider. The two players were evenly matched in the third set but it was Kartal, using a protected injury ranking to play, who managed to break Svitolina's serve at 5-4 and book her place in the last four. JCB India Opens 3S Dealership Facility In Ranchi
clusters.text: JCB India has inaugurated a new dealership facility in Ranchi, operated by Premsons Motor Udyog Pvt. Ltd., to strengthen its presence in Jharkhand. The facility will give customers in Ranchi and across the State access to JCB’s full product range, backed by sales, service and parts support. The facility covers 18,000 sq ft, has a four-bay workshop and is staffed by about 230 professionals. It will be the dealership’s headquarters, overseeing operations across 15 districts of Jharkhand. These are Ranchi, East Singhbhum, West Singhbhum, Seraikela-Kharsawan, Palamu, Latehar, Garhwa, Koderma, Hazaribagh, Chatra, Ramgarh, Gumla, Simdega, Khunti and Lohardaga. Built to JCB’s global corporate identity standards, the facility houses a fully operational LiveLink Command Centre. This is JCB’s telematics platform, which gives real-time information on machine performance, service needs, utilisation and security, and supports fleet management round the clock. It also has a rainwater harvesting system. Mr. Deepak Shetty, CEO and Managing Director of JCB India, said Jharkhand is playing a growing role in India’s infrastructure, mining and industrial growth, which creates opportunities for the construction equipment sector. He called the investment a long-term commitment to the State and praised Premsons Motor Udyog as a family-owned business that has grown alongside JCB.

also: Yogi proposes naming Prayagraj crossing after freedom fighter Masuriyadin Pasi
Yogi Adityanath Seeks to Rename Prayagraj Crossing After Freedom Fighter Masuriyadin Pasi
clusters.text:
Prayagraj, Oct 15 (PTI) Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath called for renaming a 'chouraha' (crossing) after freedom fighter Mahashay Masuriyadin Pasi as he unveiled his statue during an event at Mahashay Masuriyadin Smarak Inter College in Teliyarganj here on Thursday.

"Where the statue of Mahashay ji has been installed, I will ask the mayor to send a proposal to name that crossing after him," Adityanath said.

The chief minister said the state government would name an institution in the city after the freedom fighter and install his statue there to inspire present and future generations.

Describing Pasi as a freedom fighter whose contribution had been overlooked, Adityanath said the government was committed to preserving the memory of historical figures.

"Every great personality who raised the voice of the deprived and Dalits and worked to empower them deserves respect," he said.

Pasi was a member of the Constituent Assembly and a former MP from Phulpur. He also opposed the British-era Criminal Tribes Act, which stigmatised several communities.

Adityanath said honouring such figures was necessary to ensure that their contributions were remembered. He also assured Pasi's family that the state would protect his legacy.

Prayagraj has a sizable share of Dalit voters, including the Pasi community.

Since Adityanath became chief minister in 2017, several cities, districts, towns, and public facilities have been renamed. Major changes include renaming Allahabad to Prayagraj and Faizabad district and division to Ayodhya in 2018, and renaming Mughalsarai town and railway junction to Pandit Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Nagar and Pandit Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Junction, respectively, the same year. Faizabad railway station was renamed Ayodhya Cantt in 2021, while several railway stations in Amethi and Pratapgarh districts were renamed in 2023-24 after religious figures and historical personalities.

More recent changes and proposals in 2026 include renaming Jalalabad in Shahjahanpur district to Parashurampuri, proposing to rename Fazilnagar in Kushinagar as Pawagarh, and announcing the renaming of Bhadarsa as Bharat Nagar and Khiloni-Suchitaganj as Maa Jwala Ji Nagar Panchayat.

The government has also announced the renaming of Bhadohi district as Sant Ravidas Nagar Bhadohi. PTI KIS ASD
